items.title: PM: Move to halt UNHCR role must go through UN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Any proposal to stop the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) from managing refugee matters in Malaysia must go through the United Nations, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar told the Dewan Rakyat that UNHCR's presence in Malaysia was a legacy issue, as the government had allowed it to operate at the time. Hamzah had asked the prime minister on plans to stop UNHCR from issuing cards to refugees and instead have the government issue identification documents.

items.title: 71-year-old man claims trial to raping, sexually assaulting teenager in mall
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A 71-year-old man was charged at the Sessions Court here with raping and sexually assaulting a teenage girl in a shopping mall toilet. On the first count, Chuah is charged with raping the 18-year-old girl in the second-floor male toilet of a shopping mall here at 4.30pm on Oct 1. The charge, framed under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, carries a prison sentence of up to 20 years and whipping, upon conviction.

items.title: No decision yet on political pact for Melaka election, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan (PH) has yet to finalise any political pact for the upcoming Melaka state election, said its communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the coalition's Presidential Council had yet to make any official decision on the matter. On Oct 3, PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the coalition remained open to discussions if there was still room for negotiations with other parties.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM OCT 6, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Tuesday, with the benchmark index rising 4.32 points, or 0.26 per cent, to 1,636 points, tracking positive performance on Wall Street. The index is expected to hover between 1,630 and 1,640 points, with the local bourse potentially ripe for some bargain-hunting activity. Construction services provider SLGC made its debut on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market, opening flat at its initial public offering price of 28 sen, with 50.4 million shares changing hands.

items.title: Viral 'squeeze' Volkswagen driver charged over highway crash
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A businessman whose highway "squeeze" manoeuvre between a lorry and a jeep went viral after a crash earlier this month was charged in the magistrate's court here today with reckless driving. Muhammad Arif Nokaiah Abdullah, 38, pleaded not guilty after the charge under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 was read before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno. He was charged with driving a Volkswagen Passat recklessly and dangerously at Km91.6 of the North-South Expressway, northbound, near Ayer Hitam, at 5.30pm on Oct 1.

items.title: Empire Sushi eyes smaller towns, Sabah for next growth leg: CIMB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Empire Premium Food Bhd sees further expansion opportunities in less penetrated markets, particularly smaller towns such as Kangar, Kota Belud and Kuala Terengganu, CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said. Empire Premium opened 15 new Empire Sushi outlets in the first half of FY27, while three existing outlets were temporarily closed for upgrading works. The firm said Empire Premium continued to record healthy sales momentum in Q2 FY27.

items.title: Banks weather Middle East shock with asset quality intact
items.summary: RHB Research said Stage 2 loans had also eased, while household borrowers remained resilient. Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd, Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd and Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) were among the most sensitive to higher yields at group level, with estimated CET-1 reductions of 88, 62 and 57 basis points respectively. RHB Research said banks using the standardised approach, including Public Bank Bhd, Hong Leong Bank Bhd, Alliance Bank, Affin Bank Bhd and Bank Islam, should benefit from capital releases under Basel III reforms, cushioning much of the mark-to-market impact.

items.title: No Rohingya among 10,000 repatriated so far, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: None of the more than 10,000 Myanmar nationals repatriated from Malaysia so far was from the Rohingya community, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The programme also includes Rohingya communities, he said. Anwar said this in response to a supplementary question from Suhaizan Kaiat (PH-Pulai) on whether the 1,400 Myanmar nationals recently repatriated by a Myanmar naval vessel included Rohingya.

items.title: Myanmar citizens, school safety among issues to be raised in Dewan Rakyat today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Issues concerning the presence of Myanmar nationals in Malaysia and student safety in schools are expected to be highlighted in today's Dewan Rakyat sitting. According to the Order Paper on the Parliament portal, Suhaizan Kaiat (PH-Pulai) will ask the Prime Minister during Minister's Question Time to outline government measures addressing the long-standing presence of Myanmar nationals, including refugees and asylum seekers. Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah (PN-Indera Mahkota) will ask the prime minister why incidents threatening student safety persist in schools despite existing safety guidelines and procedures.

items.title: EC to hold special meeting tomorrow on Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting tomorrow to discuss arrangements for the 16th Melaka election. The details to be announced include the dates for the election writ, nomination day, campaign period and polling day for the 16th Melaka state election. The state legislative assembly was dissolved effective Sept 23 to pave the way for the state election.

items.title: Google, Constellation near deal for nuclear power
items.summary: CALIFORNIA: Google's parent Alphabet is nearing a multi-year deal to buy nuclear energy from Constellation Energy for US$1 billion or more, Bloomberg News reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the matter. Google could not immediately be reached for comment outside regular business hours, while Constellation Energy declined to comment. Last year, search giant Google partnered with NextEra Energy to restart an Iowa nuclear power plant.

items.title: Google faces UK court over app store charges
items.summary: LONDON: A class action lawsuit against Google opens in London Tuesday, with the technology giant accused of earning excessive commissions from its app store, impacting 20 million UK consumers and businesses. The plaintiffs, who allege Google abused its dominant position, are seeking more than £1 billion (US$1.3 billion) in damages in a hearing at the Competition Appeal Tribunal set to last seven weeks. The case concerns purchases made on the Google Play Store in the UK between October 1, 2015 and July 31, 2026.

items.title: Banking industry, PayNet to introduce industry fraud alert: Bank Negara
items.summary: Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the industry-wide fraud alert capabilities can warn banks and customers of a potential risk before the transaction is completed. Abdul Rasheed said this capability may introduce interference for customers, and there may also be complaints. "The revised risk management methodology policy document strengthens financial institutions' resilience against technology-related risks, cyber risks, and rapidly evolving digital crimes.

items.title: UN chief calls for Gaza ceasefire ahead of Oct 7 anniversary
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres on Monday called for a permanent ceasefire in Gaza ahead of the third anniversary of the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attack on Israel. And it is time to respect international law," Guterres said in a statement, calling for a "political path to lasting peace across the whole region." Guterres also said Palestinians in Gaza have faced a "massive loss of life, displacement and destruction," without specifying their death toll.

items.title: Penang seeks 2027 Budget boost for air connectivity, tourism
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang wants the 2027 Budget to prioritise air connectivity, international events and George Town's heritage to strengthen tourism and local economic benefits. Penang Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said the state urged the federal government to strengthen the tourism agenda through targeted investments. He said the initiative would complement ongoing efforts to strengthen Penang's international air links and maximise the benefits of the planned expansion of Penang International Airport (PIA).

items.title: Asian shares track Wall Street higher, Treasury yields near multi-decade highs
items.summary: MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.2 per cent, while Japan's Nikkei gained 0.7 per cent. European stock futures climbed 0.5 per cent. Nasdaq futures edged up 0.2 per cent and S&P 500 futures rose 0.1 per cent.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng cites fresh LCS delays in renewing scrutiny of Zahid’s ‘please implement’ note
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — DAP’s Lim Guan Eng today cited fresh delays to Malaysia’s Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project in renewing scrutiny of Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s role in the procurement when he was defence minister. Lim also referred to a July 8, 2010 letter from Boustead Naval Shipyard (BNS) to Ahmad Zahid, then defence minister, seeking a letter of intent from the government for the LCS project. “The words ‘please implement’ continue to haunt Ahmad Zahid Hamidi over the RM11.22 billion purchase of five LCS,” Lim said.

items.title: Gold inches lower as firmer dollar, higher yields weigh
items.summary: NEW YORK: Gold eased on Tuesday, pressured by a firmer US dollar and rising Treasury yields, though losses were limited by easing expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike this month. Spot gold slipped 0.3 per cent to US$4,128.69 per ounce by 0155 GMT. US gold futures were little changed at US$4,156.00.

items.title: Communications Ministry submits 2027 Budget wishlist to grow creative sector
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Communications Ministry has submitted its wishlist for the 2027 Budget, focusing on growing Malaysia's creative economy. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the ministry was looking beyond ongoing programmes, with greater emphasis being placed on the film, animation, music, arts and culture industries. "For our ministry, apart from ongoing programs under Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM), our departments are exploring a new dimension, namely the 'orange economy' or creative economy.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia opens higher on positive Wall Street momentum
items.summary: The index opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38. In active trade, Zetrix AI inched up half a sen to seven sen, Divfex rose one sen to 16.5 sen, Ramssol gained 2.5 sen to 86 sen, while ACE market debutant SLGC eased 3.5 sen to 24.5 sen, and Dagang NeXchange inched down half a sen to 50 sen. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index gained 41.29 points to 17,584.78, the FBM Emas Index appreciated 44.30 points to 12,234.65, the FBM Top 100 Index widened 46.09 points to 12,019.47, the FBM Emas Shariah Index advanced 39.24 points to 12,108.25, and the FBM ACE Index improved 7.73 points to 5,614.34.

items.title: After Irene Sofiya’s death, Suhakam calls for nationwide overhaul of school safeguarding
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Suhakam’s Children’s Commissioners have called for nationwide reforms to school safeguarding following the death of 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, including tighter student check-out procedures, missing-student protocols and audits of safety gaps on school grounds. In a statement today, the commissioners said schools needed to move beyond conventional security measures towards a “proactive, child-centred safeguarding culture”, particularly for activities held outside normal school hours. The recommendations come as police continue investigating Irene’s death at a school in Yong Peng, Batu Pahat, on Saturday.

items.title: Political Financing Bill may bar foreign funds, third-party contributions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The proposed Political Financing Bill may bar political parties from receiving foreign contributions, including funds channelled or managed through third parties, with the same regulatory controls applied to such funding. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the proposed scope would apply at both federal and state levels and throughout the political cycle, before, during and after elections. She said the Bill was also proposed to require political funds to be received and used through official channels that could be recorded, traced and audited.

items.title: SUPP mourns passing of party loyalist, ‘father of hawkers’ Song Swee Guan
items.summary: MIRI, Oct 6 — The Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP) has paid tribute to veteran member and former leader Datuk Song Swee Guan, who passed away Sunday at the age of 84. SUPP secretary-general Datuk Sebastian Ting said the party was deeply saddened by the passing of Kuching South’s first mayor, and extended his condolences on behalf of the leadership and all members. Ting said as Kuching South’s founding mayor in August 1988, Song helped lay the foundations for the development and administration of Kuching South, serving until 1996.

items.title: Higher education minister: 1.16 million PTPTN borrowers have RM10.7b in outstanding repayments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Some 1.16 million National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers had RM10.7 billion in outstanding loan repayments as of August 31, the Dewan Rakyat was told. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the figure represented the latest total of outstanding repayments owed to PTPTN. “The total outstanding loan repayments of the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) as of August 31, 2026 was RM10.7 billion involving 1.16 million borrowers,” he said in a written parliamentary reply.

items.title: Grappling with 'homework scams,' US universities shun AI detectors
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Locked in a cat-and-mouse struggle, biology professor Timothy Paustian devised novel ways to catch students turning in chatbot-generated assignments. But like many US universities, his institution is shunning AI detection software. Sixty out of 350 students were caught using AI.

items.title: New Bar Course expected in 2028, or 2029 at latest, says Azalina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Malaysia’s New Bar Course (NBC) is expected to be implemented in 2028, or by 2029 at the latest, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said. She said the board established the New Bar Course Task Force on April 27, 2026, to conduct a study and develop an operational framework for the NBC. Azalina said the board and the task force were taking the necessary steps towards implementation, including preparing course content modules for the Conversion Course (CC) and Legal Practice Postgraduate Certificate (LPPC) programmes, as well as a question bank.

items.title: AI Governance Bill to require safety measures for child-focused chatbots, apps
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Developers of chatbots and applications targeting children will be required to incorporate safety-by-design measures, including content filtering, under the proposed Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Bill. "For applications or chatbots targeting children, developers are required to implement safety-by-design elements," he said in a written parliamentary reply. He said the measures would include regular risk impact assessments and harmful content filtering to prevent the psychological manipulation of children.

items.title: RMAF Anka-S logs 232.7 flight hours since deployment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Malaysian Air Force's (RMAF) Anka-S Medium-Altitude Long Endurance Unmanned Aircraft System (MALE UAS) has logged 232.7 flight hours as of Sept 22. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the hours covered test flights, training, competency development, maintenance-related activities and ground system testing. He said the Anka-S could conduct surveillance for almost 24 hours, day and night, in various weather conditions.

items.title: Police seek man over mosque vandalism in Tumpat
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 6 — Police are identifying a man believed to be linked to the vandalism of the Al-Aziz Al-Hadi Mosque in Kota SPP Warisan, Tumpat, yesterday. Tumpat police chief ACP Mohd Khairi Shafie said CCTV footage from the mosque showed a man believed to be connected to the incident, which occurred at 6.35am. Mohd Khairi said police were also investigating the motive and assessing the extent of the damage or losses incurred.

items.title: Myanmar detainees underwent rigorous screening before repatriation, says Home Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: All Myanmar detainees involved in the first phase of the repatriation programme in Lumut, Perak, on Sept 29 underwent rigorous screening and verification before being returned voluntarily, safely, and with dignity to their home country. The Home Ministry said the process covered citizenship verification, documentation, health screening, and identity checks. As of Aug 31, 11,804 Myanmar citizens were detained at Immigration Detention Depots and Baitul Mahabbah facilities nationwide.

items.title: Defence minister: Strengthening cooperation, system resilience among focuses in tackling cyber threats in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Cyber threats have the potential to destroy national critical infrastructure and escalate into a national crisis. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said new forms of cyberattacks could paralyse essential systems and daily services. He said critical infrastructure at risk includes airports, ports, banking systems, healthcare facilities and internet networks.

items.title: Kulim boy, 13, seriously injured in school incident amid reported academic stress
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — A 13-year-old boy was seriously injured in an incident at a secondary school in Kulim, Kedah, with police saying he had been experiencing stress over his studies and upcoming examinations. Kulim district police chief Superintendent Syamsul Sinring said the incident occurred at about 3.40pm on Sunday during a school break. Syamsul said the boy was also worried about examinations scheduled for next week and whether he would be able to meet his parents’ expectations.

items.title: Malaysia’s border control agency seizes RM11.8m cocoa consignment from Uganda at Pasir Gudang Port
items.summary: In a statement, AKPS said the seizure of 637,000 kilogrammes of cocoa beans was made following an inspection by enforcement officers at 3.50 pm. AKPS stressed that any attempt to declare conflicting data at the country’s entry points constitutes an offence under Section 13 of the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Act 2011 [Act 728]. AKPS said it viewed such activities seriously and would continue to carry out enforcement at the country’s entry points.

items.title: 'Burglar' footsteps turn out to be sun bear foraging in housing area
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Footsteps heard in a residential area in Taman Tuanku Ja'afar around midnight on Sunday were initially mistaken for those of a burglar, but turned out to be a sun bear foraging for food. I thought it was a burglar, but a sun bear came out instead. "We set up a bear trap in the area on Sept 21 after receiving a report that a sun bear had damaged stingless bee honey hives kept inside the camp," he said when contacted today.

items.title: Home Ministry: Myanmar nationals undergo rigorous screening before repatriation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — All Myanmar nationals involved in the first phase of the repatriation programme in Lumut, Perak, on September 29 underwent rigorous screening and verification before being repatriated voluntarily, safely, and with dignity to their home country. The Home Ministry (KDN) said the process covered citizenship verification, documentation, health screening and identity checks. “As of August 31, there were 11,804 Myanmar nationals detained at Immigration Detention Depots and Baitul Mahabbah facilities nationwide,” it said.

items.title: Trump opens tax-free 'red' diesel to all buyers
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Monday signed an executive order allowing anyone to buy tax-exempt red-dyed diesel, a fuel normally reserved for farm machinery and other off-road equipment. Speaking at a rally in Nebraska, Trump told supporters the order would "officially waive the off-road requirement and allow anyone to purchase tax-free red-dyed diesel for any reason." Red-dyed diesel is essentially the same fuel as standard diesel, but it is exempt from highway fuel taxes.

items.title: Bersatu tells Perikatan to stop ‘playing victim’ as coalition feud deepens
items.summary: Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said PN should not push narratives unsupported by evidence or suggest that others were acting cowardly or oppressing the coalition without justification. “PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan needs to answer whether it is true that Bersatu lodged complaints over the management of the coalition,” he said in a statement last night. Tun Faisal said that if PAS, which administers PN, had not breached the coalition’s constitution, its leaders should produce the relevant meeting minutes, correspondence and other documents.

items.title: Police record statements in probe into 13-year-old student's fall from school building
items.summary: KULIM: Police are recording statements from several people after a 13-year-old student fell from the third floor of a secondary school here on Sunday. Kulim police chief Superintendent Syamsul Sinring said the boy was seriously injured in the incident and is still receiving treatment at Kulim Hospital. "We are recording statements from several people and no arrests have been made in the case," he said when contacted today.

items.title: Message in bottle drifts 10 years from Japan to Terengganu
items.summary: The English letter, titled "Message from Nishino" and dated Oct 2, 1989, was written by Nakamura Koichi, the principal of the Nishino Primary School. The Japanese letter was written by a 6-year-old Primary One pupil named Kowaki Yohei. With assistance from a Japanese expatriate at the Kerteh plant, Kitamura, Zulkafli translated Yohei's letter, which read: "My name is Kowaki Yohei.

items.title: Economy Ministry gets 9,955 project proposals worth RM944b for 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The Economy Ministry has received 9,955 new and extension project proposals totalling RM944 billion for 2027. The ministry said RM80.4 billion was required as the 2027 development expenditure ceiling for consideration under the development planning process. The ministry said the 13MP targets zero development projects remaining not started in the second year after approval by 2030.

items.title: AstraZeneca to invest over US$1bil in Massachusetts, boost workforce
items.summary: NEW YORK: AstraZeneca said on Monday it would spend more than US$1 billion in Massachusetts as part of its broader US$50 billion US investment plan, a move expected to expand its workforce in the state by more than 50 per cent in the coming years. The Anglo-Swedish drugmaker also opened a new research and development center in Cambridge, Massachusetts, as part of the investment. The Cambridge site joins AstraZeneca's other major US research center in Gaithersburg, Maryland.

items.title: Malaysia's rice stocks sufficient for six months, fish for 240 days
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has sufficient rice stocks to meet domestic requirements for six months, while fish stocks, managed by fishermen's associations and industry players, can last up to 240 days, says Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. Mohamad said physical rice stocks stood at 1.193 million tonnes as at Sept 30, comprising 200,000 tonnes of national rice buffer stocks and 993,478 tonnes of commercial stocks. For fish, he said stocks under the supervision of fishermen's associations stood at 247.98 tonnes as at August 31, while industry players held 9,690 tonnes.

items.title: LCS 1, LCS 2 piping, wiring work remain behind target, A-G’s report finds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Progress on piping and wiring work for Littoral Combat Ships (LCS) 1 and 2 remains behind target, putting subsequent construction activities and the targeted physical handover (PHO) of LCS 1 at risk. Meanwhile, wiring work on LCS 1 and LCS 2 had reached 51.41 per cent and 43.49 per cent, respectively, representing delays of 48.59 and 56.51 percentage points. As of July 2026, piping work on LCS 1 had reached 100 per cent, while LCS 2 stood at 96 per cent.

items.title: Malaysia haze worsens overnight as unhealthy areas nearly double to 21, Johor hardest hit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Haze conditions worsened sharply across Malaysia overnight, with 21 areas recording unhealthy air quality as of 8am today, almost double the 11 reported yesterday afternoon. Johor was the worst-affected state, accounting for eight of the unhealthy readings, according to data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS). IPD Serian in Sarawak and Johan Setia in Selangor, which had recorded unhealthy air quality yesterday afternoon, improved to moderate readings of 98 this morning.

items.title: A-G’s report: RM2.55m in allowances paid without valid authority
items.summary: Of the amount, RM2.31 million involved KWDA funds, while RM239,784 was from KWPPL. According to the report, an audit of KWDA expenditure in 2025 found that RM2.31 million was paid as allowances and facilities to the KWDA Board and officers of the Malaysian Marine Department (JLM) without valid authority. As at December 31, 2025, KWDA had a balance of RM273.12 million, with receipts totalling RM103.48 million during the year, while KWPPL recorded a balance of RM24.72 million with receipts of RM5.81 million.

items.title: E-Jamin operated without formal govt contract for five years, PAC finds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The e-Jamin system, used in 192 courts nationwide, has operated for five years since 2020 without a formal contract between the government and its operator, Dapat Vista Sdn Bhd, due to an initial interpretation that it was merely a commercial transaction. Public Accounts Committee (PAC) member Syahredzan Johan said the system was originally introduced as a Proof of Concept in 2017 before being expanded nationwide for bail payments, but was not followed by a proper government procurement process or a formal agreement. He said PAC found conflicting interpretations among government agencies regarding the status of bail funds before the matter was finalised through an official AGC review.

items.title: Kedah KPDN takes RON95 samples after claims of water-mixed fuel
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 6 — The Kedah Ministry of Domestic Trade and Costs of Living (KPDN) has taken RON95 petrol samples from 11 petrol stations in several districts for analysis following recent viral claims that the fuel was mixed with water. State KPDN director Muhammad Nizam Jamaludin said the action followed public complaints that vehicles had broken down after refuelling at the affected stations. “KPDN enforcement teams conducted inspections at 11 petrol stations today and took fuel samples from the involved tanks or pumps for inspection and further analysis.

items.title: Perikatan’s bid to challenge ROS suspension order to be heard by High Court on Oct 13
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The High Court here yesterday set October 13 to hear Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) application for leave to commence a judicial review against the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) suspension order on the coalition’s activities. PN and PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, along with secretaries-general of Parti Gerakan Rakyat Malaysia (Gerakan) Wong Chia Zhen and Malaysian Indian People’s Party (MIPP) N. Sathes Kumar, filed the application as the first to third applicants. The fourth and fifth applicants were the secretaries-general of Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan), Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah, and Parti Pejuang Tanahair (Pejuang), Datuk Sazmi Miah.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Issues on Myanmar nationals, school student safety among matters to be raised
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The presence of Myanmar nationals in Malaysia and student safety in schools are expected to be among the issues raised at today’s Dewan Rakyat sitting. According to the Order Paper on the Parliament portal, during the Minister’s Question Time, Suhaizan Kaiat (PH-Pulai) will ask the Prime Minister to outline the government’s steps to address the long-standing presence of Myanmar nationals, including refugees and asylum seekers, which has raised public concern. Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah (PN-Indera Mahkota) will ask the Prime Minister why incidents threatening student safety continue in schools despite government safety guidelines and procedures being in place.

items.title: Zetrix AI submits settlement proposal after JPJ services suspended over RM314m arrears
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Zetrix AI Berhad has submitted a proposal to the Malaysian government to address outstanding remittances after authorities suspended its Road Transport Department (JPJ) collection services over RM314 million in unpaid government revenue. “Zetrix AI has submitted a proposed solution to the Government of Malaysia to address the outstanding remittances for their consideration,” it said. Transport Minister Anthony Loke said yesterday that My E.G.

items.title: Budget 2027: What RM425m for plantations and commodities means for Malaysians
items.summary: The plantation and commodities sector The ministry oversees commodities including palm oil, rubber, cocoa, pepper, timber, kenaf, sago and tobacco, as well as related downstream activities. Cooking oil and food Palm oil is perhaps the most familiar example. Oil palm also extends to markets abroad.

items.title: IGP: Police record statements from 25 witnesses in KLIA incident involving border agency chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Police have recorded statements from 25 witnesses as part of investigations into allegations that the director-general of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) physically assaulted two police personnel at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on September 28. In a statement issued today, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said that the two officers had lodged police reports over the alleged incident. The 25 witnesses whose statements have been recorded include PDRM officers and personnel, AKPS officers, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) auxiliary police personnel, baggage-handling system workers, medical officers and independent witnesses.

items.title: Higher education minister: Universities not only path to youth success
items.summary: He said knowledge and skills in technical fields also opened up career opportunities for young people, including those who were less academically inclined. He said this during the "Technology Driving Change: Is Malaysian Talent Ready?” He said technical and engineering fields did not necessarily depend solely on degree qualifications, but also required skilled workers who had undergone engineering-related training at skills institutions.

items.title: Defence minister: LCS missile compensation claim expected to take time
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Recovering funds linked to the procurement of missiles for the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) will not be resolved immediately and will take time, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. He said that although requests for Norway’s assistance had been made at various levels, including by the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim), Foreign Minister (Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan) and himself, Norway had refused to intervene. Mohamed Khaled said the Norwegian government’s lack of intervention has left Malaysia to pursue its claim directly with the company, which he said has given various excuses.

items.title: IGP: Don’t hide school safety issues to protect reputations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Safety issues in schools should not be concealed to protect reputations, as this may prevent authorities from taking action, said Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail. Mohd Khalid said school safety is a shared responsibility requiring cooperation among PDRM, schools, the Ministry of Education, and parents. School liaison officers also regularly visit and coordinate with school authorities on safety issues.

items.title: Johor MB: State government ready to help schools review security measures following student’s death
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Oct 5 — The Johor state government is ready to review and assist with basic infrastructure needs in schools across the state to strengthen security measures, says Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi. Onn Hafiz expressed full support for any initiative implemented by the Education Ministry (MOE), particularly the installation of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in strategic areas within school premises. Meanwhile, State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said discussions would be held soon between the Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) and the Batu Pahat District Education Office (PPD).

items.title: PM Anwar: Land encroachment must be taken seriously
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Good governance practices must continue to be upheld, while any form of unauthorised land encroachment must not be taken lightly as it could affect national planning and the interests of the people, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he stressed these points while chairing the 83rd National Land Council meeting. “Land management must be carried out prudently and systematically to minimise risks to environmental sustainability,” he said.

items.title: Warehouse worker pleads not guilty to driving under the influence, injuring two marathon runners
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 —An e-commerce platform warehouse worker pleaded not guilty in the Magistrate’s Court here today to two charges of riding a motorcycle under the influence of alcohol, causing injuries to two participants of a running event last Saturday. Lawyer Muhammad Iqbal Azmi from the National Legal Aid Foundation, representing Muhammad Saiful, appealed for a bail reduction, saying that his client was single and earned RM1,500 a month. Magistrate Aliaa Anwar granted Muhammad Saiful bail of RM500 with one surety for each charge and set Jan 7, 2027, for case mention and submission of documents.

items.title: Govt launches framework to prepare communications, multimedia workforce for AI-driven changes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The federal government today launched a new framework to align communications and multimedia industry needs with education and skills development as artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation, emerging technologies and the green economy reshape the sector. Its implementation will also involve the Higher Education and Human Resources ministries to align industry needs with education and skills development. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the framework identifies industry needs while aligning government, industry and education efforts to keep talent development in step with technological and economic changes.

items.title: ‘Touch ‘n Go rep’ scam leaves Kedah woman RM150 poorer, says consumer group
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 5 — A 39-year-old self-employed woman lost about RM150, including her BUDI Madani RON95 (BUDI95) petrol subsidy and reward points, after a phone scammer posing as a Touch ‘n Go representative compromised her e-wallet. Kedah Consumers Association (Cake) president Mohamad Yusrizal Yusoff said the victim lodged a report at the association’s office yesterday. “The victim said the caller offered her a new Touch ‘n Go card with various perks, including reward points, store vouchers offering discounts of up to 80 per cent, and overseas spending capabilities.
